title: Jenga: Effective Memory Management for Serving LLM with Heterogeneity
technique: Two-level LCM-based page allocator for heterogeneous KV/state sizes (cross-attention, sliding window, Mamba, vision embeddings) plus per-layer-type prefix caching and eviction APIs, implemented on vLLM

optimized_metrics.evidence: Therefore, a new memory allocator is needed to reduce the memory waste of heterogeneous LLMs.
To lower costs, maximizing the request batch size by managing GPU memory efficiently is crucial.

headline_claim.text: Jenga improves GPU memory utilization by up to 79.6%, and increases serving throughput by up to 4.92x (1.80x on average).

reported_metrics.where: Fig 13 end-to-end throughput (req/s) on H100 and L4
Fig 14 averaged E2EL vs request rate (Llama vision)
Fig 14 (up to 29.43x lower at high load)
Fig 14 (Jenga higher than vLLM due to larger batches)
memory waste / utilization, Fig 3, decode batch size (§7.3), prefix cache hit rate

metric_definitions.definition_quote: E2EL denotes end-to-end latency, TTFT denotes time to first token, and TPOT denotes time per output token.
metric_definitions.notes: Only acronym expansions; no formal definitions or percentile. Averages.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Figure 13: End-to-end throughput. Amplified Ministral's throughput in both vLLM and Jenga by 10x for better visualization.
metric_definitions.notes: Requests/s on offline dataset replay; text never defines it formally.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: In the MMMU-pro dataset, which contains 6193 image tokens and 43 text tokens for each request on average, the resulting memory waste is 79.6%.
metric_definitions.notes: 79.6% is wasted fraction of KV memory under PagedAttention for Llama 3.2 Vision (analytic); the abstract's 'GPU memory utilization improvement up to 79.6%' reuses the same number.

load_regime: offline dataset replay for throughput; request-rate sweep for the Llama vision latency study (Fig 14)
tradeoff_acknowledged: TPOT of Jenga is larger than vLLM because it batches more requests (same TPOT if scheduling the same number of requests per step); low-rate latency differs by only 2.6%.
models: Llama 3.2 Vision, Gemma-2, Ministral, Jamba-1.5, Character.ai-style, PyramidKV, Llama 3.1
workloads: MMLU-pro, MMMU-pro, arXiv-QA, ShareGPT-style long contexts
extractor_notes: Throughput measured as req/s without any SLO or percentile; latency treated as a do-no-harm constraint (mean). Abstract 'memory utilization +79.6%' coincides numerically with the analytic waste figure of PagedAttention on one model; ambiguous whether measured improvement. Model sizes vary by platform.
load_class_quote: Offline dataset replay for the throughput study ('Figure 13: End-to-end throughput', MMLU-pro/MMMU-pro/arXiv-QA datasets) vs request-rate sweep for latency: 'Figure 14 shows the latency under different request rates of the Llama Vision model.' (§7.2)
